newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela electric tariff hike not yet ready.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela electric tariff hike not yet ready.

text.p: Long-awaited increases in Venezuelan electricity tariffs are still in the pipeline as the government continues to study potential social and inflationary impact, a government official said.
"There is still no final decision at the Executive level ...At the moment, there is no official tariff scheme in operation," Vice Minister of Energy and Mines Evanan Romero told Congress.

Romero said a final decision could be forthcoming in the next couple of weeks and that the new scheme would reduce currently steep cross-subsidies from high-paying businesses to low paying domestic users. But he added that any increases would be phased in gradually, "bearing in mind people's buying power."
State-owned electricity companies have recently added their voices to private sector calls for increases in tariffs, which have not kept up with inflation that reached triple digits last year.

Mariano Crespo, acting president for Venezuela's privatization body, the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV), told Congress the FIV alone had paid-out $10.6 billion in subsidies to state-owned electric companies over the past 23 years.
